title: Pharmacist dispensing of over-the-counter oral contraceptives to MassHealth members and HSN patients under M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83 and the MassHealth standing order
subtopic: Standing order authority, claims, protocol and dispensing record
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83(a) defines 'HSN' as the payment program established and administered in accordance with section 8A and sections 64 to 69 of chapter 118E, 'HSN patient' as an individual served by an HSN provider whose services are paid for through the HSN, and 'OTC oral contraceptive' as a nonprescription oral contraceptive approved or otherwise authorized by the United States Food and Drug Administration. Under s. 83(b), notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, a practitioner who is registered to prescribe or dispense controlled substances in the course of the practitioner's professional practice under section 7 of chapter 94C and is designated by the assistant secretary for the division may issue a standing order that may be used for a licensed pharmacist to dispense an OTC oral contraceptive to a MassHealth member or HSN patient. Under s. 83(c) a licensed pharmacist may dispense an OTC oral contraceptive in accordance with that standing order to a MassHealth member or HSN patient, and, except for gross negligence or willful misconduct, a pharmacist who, in good faith, dispenses an OTC oral contraceptive consistent with the standing order shall not be subject to any criminal or civil liability or professional disciplinary action by the board of registration in pharmacy related to that dispensing. Under s. 83(d) a pharmacist who dispenses an OTC oral contraceptive under the section to a MassHealth member or HSN patient shall submit a claim to MassHealth or the HSN, as applicable. Under s. 83(e), except for gross negligence or willful misconduct, the assistant secretary for the division or a physician who issues the standing order, and any practitioner who, acting in good faith, directly or through the standing order, prescribes or dispenses an OTC oral contraceptive to a MassHealth member or HSN patient, shall not be subject to any criminal or civil liability or professional disciplinary action; under s. 83(f) the division may adopt regulations or issue written guidance to implement the section. The MassHealth Standing Order for Prescribing and Dispensing Over-the-counter Oral Hormonal Contraceptives, signed by a physician and dated January 27, 2025, states that it is issued pursuant to M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83, which it describes as providing that a qualified practitioner designated by the assistant secretary for MassHealth may issue a standing order that may be used for a licensed pharmacist to dispense an over-the-counter (OTC) oral contraceptive to a MassHealth member or Health Safety Net (HSN) patient, and it authorizes licensed pharmacists to dispense over-the-counter oral hormonal contraceptives to any MassHealth member or HSN patient who states that they are of reproductive potential and age. It lists norgestrel 0.075 mg tablet, dispensed up to a 365-day supply, with directions to take one tablet by mouth at the same time every day and no later than three hours following the time of the previous day's dose. It states that pharmacists must follow its protocol: the patient states they are of reproductive potential and age; the pharmacist confirms the selected over-the-counter product is covered by the standing order as listed, reviews the patient profile for drug-drug interactions, counsels the patient on the contraindications, proper use and administration, and side effects the order lists, and advises the patient to follow up and consult with their primary care physician or obstetrician/gynecologist. Records of dispensing must be maintained in the patient profile of the pharmacy dispensing system.
exam_relevance: Tests that dispensing an over-the-counter oral contraceptive to a MassHealth member or HSN patient under the MassHealth standing order rests on M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83 rather than on pharmacist prescribing under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F, together with the order's covered product, supply, protocol, claim and record.

common_confusions: Treating dispensing under the MassHealth standing order as pharmacist prescribing under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F; the order is issued pursuant to M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83.
Extending the standing order beyond MassHealth members and HSN patients, or beyond the over-the-counter product it lists.
Overlooking the claim duty in s. 83(d) and the order's statement that records of dispensing must be maintained in the patient profile of the pharmacy dispensing system.
verification_notes: Read M.G.L. c. 118E, s. 83, and s. 84, which shares its definitions, on malegislature.gov, and located the insertion of both sections by St. 2024, c. 140, s. 132; read the full two-page MassHealth standing order linked as 'Oral Contraceptive Standing Order' from the Standing Orders and Other Documents list on the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Practice Resources page on mass.gov, including the signature above the physician signature line and the date January 27, 2025, on 2026-09-16.
